newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends up 1/8 to 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends up 1/8 to 1/4.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market ended Friday up an 1/8 to 1/4 overall, as a next week's supply begins to take center stage.
Dollar bonds were up an 1/8 to 1/4, while high grade bonds were overall unchanged.
There was light to moderate secondary activity, traders said, adding that the overall market was up an 1/8 to 1/4.

While the market handily absorbed almost all of the $4.4 billion slated for sale this week -- which included bonds from Puerto Rico and Pennsylvania and Connecticut -- Thursday's indigestion did erode prices, especially in the Treasury market.

John Nuveen & Co, however, said Friday in its weekly municipal market comment that "municipals held up well in comparison, with the Bond Buyer 20 retreating just 5 basis points to reach 5.75 percent on Thursday."

The weekly report also remarked on the week's supply: "Rather than exert excessive downward pressure on prices, the flood of paper seemed simply to draw in more participants. Casualty companies were particularly active this week, attracted by the large blocks of high grade, recognizable names."
Municipal bond sales for next week are expected to total $3.7 billion in 115 sales.
Negotiated offerings total $1.9 billion in 45 sales, with a $316 million Palm Beach County, Fla., deal through Smith Barney topping the list.
On the competitive side, 70 sales totaling $1.8 billion are on the schedule, a $525 million California deal on Tuesday is the largest.
An additional seven sales totaling $407 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds next week, depending on market conditions.

In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed up 9/32 at 112-24/32. The June T-bond contract was up 11/32 at 108-27/32. The MOB spread was 125 ticks down two ticks from the close of 127 on Thursday.
